facts.x86_to_arm_notes: REPLACE the x86 hook mechanism. x86 wrote `E9 rel32` + 5 NOPs over the entry (write_relative_jump); do NOT port that. On ARM the three sites are std::function<void()> _Do_call bodies (vtable slot 2 = byte offset +8) of three lambda _Func_impl classes, so there are two equivalent plans: (A, RECOMMENDED) overwrite the single vtable cell with the host function pointer (cell is in .data, PAGE_READWRITE, no code patching, works on W^X-strict systems incl. Windows RT, no FlushInstructionCache needed): `void** cell=(void**)(image+CELL_RVA); require(*cell == (void*)(image+FN_RVA+1)); VirtualProtect(cell,4,PAGE_READWRITE,&old); *cell=(void*)hook /*bit0 already set for a Thumb C function*/; restore protection`. (B, fallback) 8-byte Thumb-2 absolute-jump trampoline at the function entry (function is 4-byte aligned and >= 18 bytes): bytes `DF F8 00 F0` (= ldr.w pc,[pc,#0]) followed by the 32-bit literal `(DWORD)hook | 1` little-endian at entry+4; VirtualProtect(entry, 8, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE) + FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), entry, 8). The literal is read from Align(entry+4,4) = entry+4 because the entry is 4-aligned. Replacement signature: `static void win32_request_xxx(void* lambda_self)` plain AAPCS (remove __attribute__((thiscall))); `lambda_self` is the std::function impl object: lambda_self+4 = adapter, adapter+4 = controller (identical to x86 get_mouse_mode_controller, so get_mouse_mode_controller() can be ported 1:1: object+4 -> adapter, adapter+4 -> controller, IsBadReadPtr probes unchanged). Return value unused (void _Do_call). The hook runs wherever the dispatcher runs the std::function (the AppPlatform_Winrt::vf18/19/22 front-ends hand it to sub_589590, the RunAsync wrapper that the host dispatcher patch owns). Semantics to keep in the replacement (same as x86): do nothing to actual; `if (controller && controller[0xa0]==0) *(int*)(controller+0x28)=1;` plus host bookkeeping (initial_menu_cursor_guard branch, host_relative_requested=TRUE, mouse_clip_dirty=TRUE). Large enough for the 8-byte trampoline: yes (24 bytes). Vtable cell RVA 0x01369c30 holds 0x0098e93d (VA at preferred base, Thumb bit set) = image+0x58e93c+1. NOTE the first 12 bytes of the relative and toggle functions are IDENTICAL (2d e9 00 48 eb 46 43 68 5a 68 92 f8); to distinguish them check 16 bytes (byte 14 differs: 0x33 vs 0x0b) or, better, the vtable cell value.

facts.x86_to_arm_notes: REPLACE the x86 hook mechanism. x86 wrote `E9 rel32` + 5 NOPs over the entry (write_relative_jump); do NOT port that. On ARM the three sites are std::function<void()> _Do_call bodies (vtable slot 2 = byte offset +8) of three lambda _Func_impl classes, so there are two equivalent plans: (A, RECOMMENDED) overwrite the single vtable cell with the host function pointer (cell is in .data, PAGE_READWRITE, no code patching, works on W^X-strict systems incl. Windows RT, no FlushInstructionCache needed): `void** cell=(void**)(image+CELL_RVA); require(*cell == (void*)(image+FN_RVA+1)); VirtualProtect(cell,4,PAGE_READWRITE,&old); *cell=(void*)hook /*bit0 already set for a Thumb C function*/; restore protection`. (B, fallback) 8-byte Thumb-2 absolute-jump trampoline at the function entry (function is 4-byte aligned and >= 18 bytes): bytes `DF F8 00 F0` (= ldr.w pc,[pc,#0]) followed by the 32-bit literal `(DWORD)hook | 1` little-endian at entry+4; VirtualProtect(entry, 8, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE) + FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), entry, 8). The literal is read from Align(entry+4,4) = entry+4 because the entry is 4-aligned. Replacement signature: `static void win32_request_xxx(void* lambda_self)` plain AAPCS (remove __attribute__((thiscall))); `lambda_self` is the std::function impl object: lambda_self+4 = adapter, adapter+4 = controller (identical to x86 get_mouse_mode_controller, so get_mouse_mode_controller() can be ported 1:1: object+4 -> adapter, adapter+4 -> controller, IsBadReadPtr probes unchanged). Return value unused (void _Do_call). The hook runs wherever the dispatcher runs the std::function (the AppPlatform_Winrt::vf18/19/22 front-ends hand it to sub_589590, the RunAsync wrapper that the host dispatcher patch owns). Semantics to keep: `*(int*)(controller+0x28)=2; initial_menu_cursor_guard=FALSE; host_relative_requested=FALSE; mouse_clip_dirty=TRUE`. Large enough for the 8-byte trampoline: yes, but only 18 bytes (do not use a 10-byte patch + anything longer than 18). Vtable cell RVA 0x01369c14 holds 0x0098e8f1 = image+0x58e8f0+1. Its first 12 bytes are unique (ends 02 22 5b 68 = movs r2,#2; ldr r3,[r3,#4]).
